points.description: States that a static array is initialised only once (not every time the function runs). Equivalent wording such as 'initialised one time only' or 'the initial values are set once and kept' earns the mark.
States the contrast: a non-static array is initialised again each time the function is called. Accept equivalent wording such as 'a non-static local array is re-created on every call'.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both the static array being initialised once and the non-static array being initialised on every call, since the question asks for a difference. The model answer only states the static half, so P2 is the implied contrast the question asks for, and it is worth less. A student who gives only the static behaviour gets P1 (3/5). Do not award P1 for vague statements such as 'static arrays are special' or 'they stay in memory' without the one-time initialisation idea.
